title: A runtime instanceof and a modifier check

blocks.text: `instanceof` needs its type at compile time. When the type comes from configuration you only have a `Class` object, and `Class.isInstance(obj)` is the runtime equivalent: it is **polymorphic** (subclasses and implemented interfaces count) and **`null` is an instance of nothing**. A manual `obj.getClass() == type` misses subtypes.
`getModifiers()` returns an `int` bitmask; `java.lang.reflect.Modifier` decodes it. Mind that an **interface carries the abstract bit** too.

items: `accepts(type, value)`: whether `value` is an instance of `type`.
`isAbstractClass(type)`: whether `type` is an abstract **class** (not an interface).
`modifiers(type)`: the modifiers as Java source spells them, in `Modifier.toString` order.

cases.says: A String is accepted by String and refused by Integer; AbstractList is an abstract class and String is not; the modifiers read "public final" and "abstract static".
A StringBuilder is accepted by CharSequence, and a Long by Number.
null is accepted by no type, and asking does not throw.
Runnable carries the abstract modifier, yet isAbstractClass(Runnable.class) is false.

concepts: Class.isInstance(obj) is the runtime instanceof: polymorphic, and false for null.
getModifiers() returns a bitmask that java.lang.reflect.Modifier decodes.
